title: Gauss-sum DFT identity makes M(n) an extreme value with FLAT amplitudes — phase-only
evidence: Exact complex probe scripts/probes/_407_conn/_C053_gaussphase_relation_moment.py and _C053_phase_coherence.py, at PRIZE-REGIME proper-subgroup primes (q,n,m=(q-1)/n): (97,8,12),(193,8,24),(337,16,21),(1153,16,72),(3137,16,196),(12289,16,768), n<sqrt(q), odd-part(m)>1 (Fermat trap excluded). THREE separate claims tested. (A) Gauss-DFT identity PROVEN exact (and is the in-tree axiom-clean SubgroupGaussSumMoment + Mathlib gaussSum norm substrate): max||tau(chi)|-sqrt(q)| <= 8e-11, max|eta_b-(1/m)*sum chibar(b)tau(chi)| <= 8e-12 over all b. Consequently B=max_b|eta_b| = (sqrt(q)/m)*P EXACTLY (|B-B_via| <= 4e-12 every case), where P=max_b|sum_t u_t chibar(b)| is a PURE unit-phase exponential sum (u_t=tau(chi_t)/sqrt(q), |u_t|=1 for the m-1 nontrivial chi). So the flat-amplitude phase-sum decomposition is REAL. (B) The connection's substituted MOMENT identity m^r*N0/q^(r/2) == M_r := sum_{chi_1...chi_r=1, chi_i in mu_n^perp} u_{chi_1}...u_{chi_r} is REFUTED: r=2 gives m^2 N0/q=11.876 vs M_r=11.010 (off ~0.87 EVERY prime: M_2 ~ m-1 exactly), and r=3 gives N0=0 (so LHS=0) vs M_r ~ -sqrt(q) NONZERO (q=97:-9.65; q=337:-18.25; q=3137:-55.97 ~ -sqrt(q)). Root cause: mu_n^perp ALWAYS contains the trivial character chi_0 with tau(chi_0)=-1, so u_{chi_0}=-1/sqrt(q) is NOT unit-modulus; the amplitude does NOT 'drop out entirely', and the (m-1)-sized chi_0-term is exactly the discrepancy. The 'PERFECTLY FLAT amplitudes / N0 is a pure moment of UNIT phases' framing is FALSE as stated. (C) Even after correcting to B=(sqrt(q)/m)*P, the residual is NOT simplified: P/sqrt(m*ln m) is STABLE ~1.1-1.4 while P/m -> 0 (0.55,0.43,0.52,0.29,0.18,0.11) so P does cancel to sqrt(m log m) (=> B~sqrt(n log m), matching the house law), but P/P_rand (vs an i.i.d. random unit-phase family) ~ 0.87-1.41 ~ 1 -- the Gauss phases {u_t} behave like a generic random unit-phase family. That 'incoherent enough' = Katz/Rojas-Leon equidistribution is PRECISELY the W-BGK/W-Betti wall the connection itself names. Amplitude-inertness (true only for the m-1 nontrivial chars) RELOCATES the sqrt-cancellation of B onto the sqrt-cancellation of the phase sum P -- the identical 25-year-open BGK/Paley problem, not a reduction past it.
honest_note: PARTIAL: the algebraic decomposition piece (A) is genuinely proven/substrate-backed (eta_b is a flat-amplitude m-1-term unit-phase sum after stripping chi_0; B=(sqrt(q)/m)P exact). But (B) the specific 'N0 = pure moment of unit phases' identity as written in the connection is FALSE -- the trivial character's amplitude 1/sqrt(q) does not drop out -- and (C) the headline 'isolates the open core to phase-only' provides no simplification: phase-coherence of {u_t} IS Katz/Rojas-Leon equidistribution = the W-BGK/W-Betti wall, empirically the phases are as coherent as random, so the open core is unchanged. Item (B) is a documented refutation candidate for DISPROOF_LOG (the unit-phase moment identity must INCLUDE the non-unit chi_0 term, i.e. M_r is a moment over mu_n^perp with one amplitude-1/sqrt(q) phase, not perfectly flat). Numerics are exact complex arithmetic, n<=16 (n=32 cases timed out at the gauss-sum O(m*q) cost in pure Python but the n=16, m up to 768 cases already span the prize-shape n<<sqrt(q)); no asymptotic n=2^30 claim. Did NOT attempt Lean (the corrected identity is not a clean already-isolated lemma -- it needs the chi_0 carve-out).
reduced_to: After the chi_0 carve-out, the prize is: does the (m-1)-term unit-phase sum P=max_b|sum_{nontrivial chi in mu_n^perp} u_t chibar(b)| exhibit sqrt(m log m) cancellation (u_t=tau(chi)/sqrt(q))? Empirically YES (P/sqrt(m log m)~1.1-1.4), and this is equivalent to Katz/Rojas-Leon equidistribution of the Gauss phases = the BGK/Paley-eigenvalue wall. No strictly cleaner OPEN statement than the existing GaussPeriodMomentBound / GeneralizedPaleyRamanujan faces; this welds back to them.
wall: W-BGK (Paley-graph / Katz-Rojas-Leon equidistribution of Gauss phases); also W-Betti (the only relations among chi_i are Hasse-Davenport, as the connection states).
